claim: Native input-readiness diagnosis; no production or harness change and no new browser execution.
nativeContract: Mouse down chooses an existing capture or the compositor-backed root input hit test; it takes implicit capture until release.
Button release needs prior pressed state, initial left button, and a second compositor-backed hit test inside the button subtree. Lost focus/capture clears pressed state.
paint_button first checks shell.updating, then flush_inspector_drafts. Flush focuses canvas and returns false only if at least one currently live inspector draft remains dirty.
The gradient-entry apply callback closes the modal before entering gradient edit, so the unchanged visible modal establishes that callback did not execute.
Native pointer-over derives from actual input hit testing and refreshes the resting pointer when the compositor publishes a scene; capture disagreement suppresses pointer-over.
inference: Stale compositor hit-test geometry is the strongest supported explanation when combined with the trace screencast timing reviewed separately by gradient_parity. The actual historical native press target was not recorded, so exact routing cannot be proven from this report.
unsupportedAlternatives: No evidence supports a dirty-draft/IME validation rejection: storage draftDirty is false and all captured paint text values/composition states are unchanged.
No native capture-loss or button-pressed diagnostic existed in this executed runtime, so a transient capture/focus interruption cannot be conclusively excluded.
proposedReadinessCheck: Expose public native InputElement.is_pointer_over and Button.is_pressed read-only in chrome diagnostics. Move the real pointer to the fresh paint button, wait up to the existing bounded deadline for native hover, then perform exactly one down/up activation. Preserve original failure evidence and all outcome assertions; no retries, synthetic click, fixed sleep, or threshold relaxation.
